quotes.text: Monitor your Android apps on Stripe SmartPOS Android devices.
After you deploy your app, you can monitor its deployment progress using the Stripe Dashboard.
This allows you to investigate any issues during deployment and to deploy a new app, if needed.

old_evidence.text: choose the release version to view the deployment status and number of Stripe readers in that status.
The app has been served to the device and will attempt to install on the next reboot.

findings: November still gives factual high-level guidance: after Android app deployment to Stripe SmartPOS devices, an operator monitors progress in Stripe Dashboard, investigates issues and can deploy a new app if needed. Troubleshooting is the only related link and is unchanged.

May also documents the exact Dashboard path (Terminal > Software > choose app > App info > select release version), per-release reader counts by status, and Pending, Served, Installed and Failed definitions. November omits those specifics; this does not establish that they were removed from the product.
The mapped summary preserves the May route and statuses, but Served should be conditional on an installation attempt at the next reboot. An Installed result is separately recorded.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 1, 2026 full monitoring workflow and four per-reader status definitions as dated authority. November 7, 2026 confirms the high-level Dashboard monitoring and investigation purpose, but gives no detail on the route or individual status behavior.
conflicts: The mapped status table says a Served app 'installs on next reboot'. The May raw says it will attempt installation at the next reboot. Keep successful installation reserved for Installed and failure for an installation error.
unresolved_questions: The shorter November capture does not settle whether the old Dashboard route and status definitions remain exactly the same in deployed product.

source_assessments.reason: Correct the existing Served-state success implication and date both captures. Retain the May detailed reporting and the November general purpose, add a reciprocal concept link and a troubleshooting route.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/monitor, November 7, 2026 still documents a fleet operator using Stripe Dashboard after deploying an Android app to Stripe SmartPOS Android devices to monitor progress, investigate issues and deploy a new app if needed. It routes to Troubleshooting and supplies no detailed Dashboard prerequisites or state definitions (new raw lines 5-13). May 1, 2026 describes the same purpose and adds the exact Dashboard Terminal > Software > app details > App info > release version path and counts of readers per status. Pending means the device has not checked the backend; Served means it received the app and will attempt installation at the next reboot; Installed marks successful installation; Failed marks an error during the installation attempt (old raw lines 6-21). source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-monitor summarizes these historical details but incorrectly makes Served sound like guaranteed installation on reboot.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/monitor, retain May 1, 2026 as the detailed factual authority and November 7, 2026 as factual but narrower monitoring evidence in source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-monitor. November retains high-level Dashboard monitoring and investigation after deployment and the existing Troubleshooting route. Its omission of the step-by-step UI, release-level reader counts and four-status table is a capture content reduction and does not establish a runtime or UI removal (new raw lines 7-13, old raw lines 6-25). Independently correct the mapped source so Served means an installation attempt on the next reboot, with success and error represented by Installed and Failed respectively (new raw line 9, old raw lines 18-21). Preserve the already-linking stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices concept route, add a reciprocal link from the source and keep the existing Troubleshooting destination as navigation.
